scope: Normalized planning catalog from supplied exports plus selected already-reviewed RHDS guidance. Not a complete WCAG conformance checklist; no application testing performed.
roleSummaries: Own accessible interaction and presentation intent.
Own accessible product composition and behavior.
Own safe component APIs and documented boundaries.
Versioned contract → tested primitives and guidance
Own verification scope, evidence and retest.
Coverage plan → findings, evidence and retest
Own inclusive participation and observed task needs.
Access plan → observed barriers and learning
Own linguistic/direction review with implementation partners.
LOC01–03; translated names, alternatives, media and data
Own scope, resources, current policies and unresolved release decisions.
Approved baseline → owned residual barriers and upkeep

checks.title: Page and embedded titles
checks.check: Give each page a descriptive title. Name iframes and embedded media according to their purpose; do not use one generic label for unrelated embeds.
checks.evidence: Rendered title and accessible embed name in context.

checks.title: Heading hierarchy
checks.check: Write headings that introduce real sections and reflect their relationships. Check rendered heading structure; treat a single h1 as a product convention, rather than an automatic WCAG test.
checks.evidence: Outline, rendered headings and relationship review.

checks.title: Reading and focus order
checks.check: Preserve meaning and operability in visual, DOM, screen-reader and sequential focus order. They need not be mechanically identical; explicitly document meaningful differences.
checks.evidence: Annotated order and observed reading/focus journey.

checks.title: Landmarks and bypass routes
checks.check: Use appropriate native sections/landmarks and a suitable mechanism to bypass repeated blocks. Avoid redundant landmarks and unnecessary region proliferation.
checks.evidence: Landmark/heading navigation and bypass test.

checks.title: Findability and consistent navigation
checks.check: Use consistent navigation, terminology and identifiable calls to action. Offer a useful contents/navigation aid for long material where appropriate.
checks.evidence: Navigation inventory and task-based finding exercise.

checks.title: Clear, inclusive wording
checks.check: Use clear, respectful language; explain unfamiliar acronyms for the audience. Readability and style guidance must be distinguished from an A/AA failure.
checks.evidence: Editorial review with intended readers and terminology list.

checks.title: Useful links and action names
checks.check: Describe destination or action clearly in context. Visible labels should support speech input; accessible names should include the visible label where required.
checks.evidence: Visible/name comparison and contextual link review.

checks.title: Unexpected navigation
checks.check: Avoid surprising context changes. Explain unusual behavior when needed; opening all links in one window and warning on every off-site link are not universal A/AA requirements.
checks.evidence: Navigation and new-context behavior observed.

checks.title: Text rather than images of text
checks.check: Use real text where the required presentation can be achieved with it; account for applicable exceptions and meaningful image descriptions.
checks.evidence: Content review and zoom/translation behavior.

checks.title: Contextual text alternatives
checks.check: Identify informative, functional, complex and decorative images, SVGs, icons and grouped images. Write alternatives conveying purpose, rather than merely checking that an alt attribute exists.
checks.evidence: Asset purpose inventory and rendered accessible names/text alternatives.

checks.title: Complex visualization meaning
checks.check: Provide the information or functional equivalent needed to understand charts and diagrams. Decide what needs a short alternative, detailed description, data view or another accessible interaction.
checks.evidence: Equivalent interpretation/task with alternative presentation.

checks.title: Captions, transcripts and descriptions
checks.check: Identify audio-only, video-only, synchronized, live and prerecorded media. Supply applicable alternatives, captions and audio description; verify accuracy and meaningful sounds, not just file presence.
checks.evidence: Media inventory and human review of equivalent information.

checks.title: Player and autoplay controls
checks.check: Make player controls keyboard operable and named. Check audio autoplay and pause/stop/hide requirements for moving content under their actual applicability conditions.
checks.evidence: Playback/control journey, timing and state observations.

checks.title: Motion preferences and flashing
checks.check: Specify meaningful motion, honor reduced-motion preferences and test them. Assess flashing thresholds separately from animation style and reduced-motion support.
checks.evidence: Preference on/off recording and flashing assessment where relevant.

checks.title: Contrast in real states
checks.check: Measure applicable text and non-text contrast against actual backgrounds, including images, states and themes. Distinguish AA minimums, AAA targets and disabled/decorative exceptions.
checks.evidence: Computed/rendered foreground-background values and state captures.

checks.title: Information beyond color
checks.check: Provide a non-color cue for meaningful status, charts, links and controls; verify the cue remains understandable in context.
checks.evidence: Grayscale/forced-colors review plus semantic state inspection.

checks.title: Resize, reflow and zoom
checks.check: Allow text enlargement to 200% and separately verify reflow at the applicable narrow viewport (typically 320 CSS px for horizontal writing). Preserve content/function and account for two-dimensional content exceptions. Do not treat no fixed widths as the criterion.
checks.evidence: Measured viewport/text scale, content and control operation.

checks.title: Typography and text spacing
checks.check: Choose legible typography and permit user text-spacing overrides without loss. Minimum body font, avoiding all-caps/thin faces/justification and prescribed line-height are design policies unless a specific requirement is demonstrated.
checks.evidence: Spacing override result and editorial/design review.

checks.title: Forced colors and user preferences
checks.check: Test OS/browser forced colors and applicable contrast/theme preferences. Preserve meaning, focus and controls; images versus CSS backgrounds alone cannot establish support.
checks.evidence: Real preference environment and observed states.

checks.title: Orientation and responsive task parity
checks.check: Support orientation unless essential and preserve essential information/function across responsive variants. Different layouts need not be pixel-identical.
checks.evidence: Portrait/landscape and narrow/wide task outcomes.

checks.title: Native semantics and behavior
checks.check: Choose native action/navigation/form elements where suitable. Match exposed role, name, value and state to behavior; avoid arbitrary div-count rules and redundant ARIA.
checks.evidence: Rendered semantics and representative interaction tests.

checks.title: Keyboard pattern and escape
checks.check: Complete essential tasks using keyboard only. Use the actual widget pattern and variant for key expectations; distinguish navigation, selection and activation. No inaccessible keyboard traps.
checks.evidence: Key sequence, focus/state evidence and successful task completion.

checks.title: Visible and unobscured focus
checks.check: Keep keyboard focus discernible and not entirely obscured by author-created content under AA. Separate stronger product policy and AAA focus requirements.
checks.evidence: Focus captures across states, sticky content and overlays.

checks.title: Modal and nonmodal overlays
checks.check: Choose a modal, disclosure, popover or tooltip contract deliberately. For modal dialogs, choose context-appropriate initial focus, keep background content inert and restore focus suitably. Do not impose a modal trap on every overlay.
checks.evidence: Open/interact/close journey with keyboard and selected AT.

checks.title: Hidden and disabled states
checks.check: Prevent focus reaching content intended to be unavailable. Distinguish visually hidden AT text, collapsed content, inert content, native disabled and aria-disabled patterns; some disabled composite items intentionally remain focusable.
checks.evidence: Focus/reading tree and activation checks for each state.

checks.title: Scrollable regions and standard behavior
checks.check: Ensure needed content can be reached and scrolled by keyboard. Add a focus stop only when needed by the implementation/support matrix, with a useful name where appropriate. Preserve expected browser scrolling and navigation.
checks.evidence: Keyboard scrolling and reachability across supported browsers.

checks.title: Target size and pointer alternatives
checks.check: Check AA minimum target size/spacing and exceptions; distinguish AAA/product larger-target policies. Provide applicable simple-pointer alternatives to multipoint/path gestures and dragging, separately from keyboard support.
checks.evidence: Measured hit regions, spacing and alternative interaction tasks.

checks.title: Predictable activation and focus
checks.check: Avoid unexpected changes on focus/input and unjustified autofocus. Define intentional route/step focus changes. Hover/focus content must satisfy applicable dismissible, hoverable and persistent conditions.
checks.evidence: Focus/input/hover journey and context-change record.

checks.title: Dynamic status and updates
checks.check: Identify actual status messages and an appropriate programmatic mechanism without unnecessary interruption. Error association, invalid state and announcement are separate. Do not announce every DOM update or force all errors into alert regions.
checks.evidence: State transition and human AT observation; source/tree evidence alone is partial.

checks.title: Timing and progressive disclosure
checks.check: Avoid unnecessary time limits and provide adjustment where required. Make loading more/revealing content discoverable, preserve position and keep key information reachable. Load-more versus infinite scroll is a design decision to verify.
checks.evidence: Timed task and continuation/recovery journey.

checks.title: Labels, groups and instructions
checks.check: Provide meaningful names plus visible labels/instructions where applicable; group related controls when needed. Test label activation and programmatic association, including custom-element hosts. Label placement is a design choice.
checks.evidence: Visible labels, accessible names, relationships and pointer activation.

checks.title: Error identification and recovery
checks.check: Identify errors in text, associate guidance with controls and expose invalid/required state as appropriate. Provide suggestions and necessary safeguards for consequential submissions. Preserve usable recovery.
checks.evidence: Invalid→correction→submit journey and state/error association.

checks.title: Efficient forms and accessible authentication
checks.check: Collect only necessary information, break up complex tasks sensibly and use applicable input-purpose/autocomplete support. Review repeated entry and cognitive authentication barriers; a honeypot is not a universal replacement for CAPTCHA.
checks.evidence: Complete/repeat/authentication task and alternative path.

checks.title: Data meaning and understandable headers
checks.check: Confirm a data table is appropriate; simplify relationships and write useful column/row headers, units and contextual identification/caption as needed.
checks.evidence: Data model and interpretation exercise with representative content.

checks.title: Programmatic table relationships
checks.check: Use table/header/data-cell markup and appropriate header associations. Handle multi-level headers explicitly when needed. Avoid layout tables and unnecessary grid roles for static data.
checks.evidence: DOM/accessibility inspection and AT header association checks.

checks.title: Responsive and localized tables
checks.check: Keep relationships understandable while resizing/localizing. A two-dimensional table may scroll in its own region; keep surrounding content reflowing and make required scrolling keyboard accessible.
checks.evidence: Narrow/zoom/long-label variants and keyboard scrolling.

checks.title: Interactive data operations
checks.check: Specify names, sort/filter/selection state, keyboard model and status updates for interactive tables. Use grid behavior only when that pattern is intentionally selected and fully supported.
checks.evidence: Sort/filter/select task and AT state/results observations.

checks.title: Language and direction metadata
checks.check: Declare the actual page language and applicable changes in language; support direction and bidirectional content. A CMS core-language list must not determine whether a language can be identified in HTML.
checks.evidence: Rendered lang/dir and mixed-language/direction review.

checks.title: Translated accessible content
checks.check: Translate relevant labels, alternatives, instructions, errors, captions and accessible-only strings as well as visible copy; preserve meaningful names and label matching.
checks.evidence: Per-locale inventory and language-qualified review.

checks.title: Localized flow and presentation
checks.check: Check destinations, offers, dates/numbers, truncation, line breaks and expansion with representative locales/directions. Validate language fallback and form expectations rather than checking translation presence only.
checks.evidence: Locale-specific journey, long-string/RTL screenshots and destination checks.

checks.title: Consumer versus component obligations
checks.check: Record accessible defaults, slots/props, naming, focus/state and consumer duties for each versioned component. Use PF/RHDS/Felt provider docs; valid API use alone does not establish accessible composition.
checks.evidence: Versioned contract with examples and responsibility boundary.

checks.title: React and Web Component runtime evidence
checks.check: Verify actual semantics and focus across portals, slots, Shadow DOM, ElementInternals and form association where used. Detect capabilities/versions; preserve known tooling limitations without rewriting correct components to appease a scanner.
checks.evidence: Real browser fixture, composed focus/relationships and selected AT test.

checks.title: Accessible authoring defaults
checks.check: Make approved building blocks easy to use correctly and document required author inputs. For applicable authoring tools, review authoring-interface accessibility and support for accessible output separately.
checks.evidence: Authoring journey, generated artifact review and safeguards.

checks.title: Identify users, barriers and essential tasks
checks.check: Plan with disabled people and varied access strategies. Record needs and barriers alongside task IDs; user stories/personas are hypotheses or reference material, not observed research evidence.
checks.evidence: Research plan, recruitment rationale and traced task needs.

checks.title: Accessible research participation
checks.check: Arrange accessible invitations, consent/materials, tools, accommodations and session methods with participants. Capture actual task barriers and distinguish study observations from expert conformance findings.
checks.evidence: Participation/access plan and consented study observations.

checks.title: Source and rendered semantic review
checks.check: Inspect rendered DOM/accessible semantics, validate relevant markup and triage real defects. A validator score, DOM inspection or accessibility snapshot alone does not prove AT behavior or conformance.
checks.evidence: Scoped findings with source/tree evidence and human triage.

checks.title: Automated scanning and regression tests
checks.check: Run installed, versioned checks against applicable routes and states; record scope, profile and limitations. Correctly distinguish violations, best practices and manual review; test regressions in real supported runtimes.
checks.evidence: Executed scan/test output with environment, route/state and coverage gaps.

checks.title: Human assistive-technology journeys
checks.check: Select browser/OS/AT combinations for product needs. Complete essential tasks and record speech/reading, operation and recovery. A screenshot, simulated persona or passing axe scan cannot substitute.
checks.evidence: Observed tasks with versions, settings, results and limitations.

checks.title: Browser, device and state coverage
checks.check: Keep a dated product support matrix of actual browser/OS/device/viewport versions. Check responsive behavior and representative interaction states; visual regression services cover only the checks they actually perform.
checks.evidence: Executed environment/state matrix with Not tested where missing.

checks.title: Findings, ownership and retest
checks.check: Separate impact, confidence, requirement type and release priority. Record target/state/method, owner, evidence, N/A reason and Not tested gaps; retest corrections against stable IDs.
checks.evidence: Versioned finding history and explicit residual coverage.

checks.title: Policy and standards baseline
checks.check: Record the project-approved standards/version and additional product policies. Preserve historical 2.1 wording as source context; use proposed WCAG 2.2 A/AA profile without asserting a current corporate/legal mandate.
checks.evidence: Approved profile and authority/source/date ledger.

checks.title: Adoption and outcome learning
checks.check: Monitor use, contributions, completion/coverage and observed task barriers. Historical download/survey targets are planning ideas, not current acceptance criteria or evidence of accessibility.
checks.evidence: Owned review cadence and meaningful outcome/usage measures.

checks.title: Approved copy and artwork
checks.check: Compare against approved copy/artwork, character counts, images, text sizes, spacing, color and hover designs. Approval does not establish accessibility.
checks.evidence: Versioned spec comparison and relevant captures.

checks.title: Brand and editorial conventions
checks.check: Check sentence case, punctuation, Red Hat nonbreaking treatment, registration marks and superscript conventions using the current brand policy. Do not treat these as WCAG rules.
checks.evidence: Brand/editorial review against current policy.

checks.title: Links and offer routing
checks.check: Verify intended destinations, destination-page links, offer IDs, downloads and lead routing. Verify the accessible link purpose under TXT02 separately.
checks.evidence: Clicked destination and form-submission outcomes.

checks.title: Drupal routing and publishing
checks.check: Apply product-specific internal node references, page/admin naming, taxonomy and shared-node preservation only in relevant publishing environments.
checks.evidence: CMS configuration and rendered destination checks.

checks.title: Analytics and personalization
checks.check: Validate the applicable tactic ID rules, analytics attributes, language policy and personalization frequency. Obtain current product rules; the supplied IDs and parameter conventions are historical examples.
checks.evidence: Product analytics/debug evidence and personalization scenario.

checks.title: URLs and SEO metadata
checks.check: Verify intended URL, metadata title/description/image and applicable structured data. Share the descriptive page-title check with STR01; do not duplicate its accessibility result.
checks.evidence: Rendered metadata and approved URL comparison.

checks.title: Asset hosting and image budgets
checks.check: Use approved asset hosts and appropriate compression/responsive delivery. The 250 KB limit is a supplied site policy, not a universal accessibility threshold.
checks.evidence: Asset URLs, encoded sizes and rendering quality.

checks.title: Performance and resource delivery
checks.check: Reduce unnecessary code and blocking work; optimize font delivery without dropping required characters/languages. Performance affects access but is not itself a WCAG pass/fail proxy.
checks.evidence: Measured load behavior and glyph/language coverage.

checks.title: PWA and offline requirements
checks.check: Use service workers/offline caching and install metadata only when product needs justify them; check freshness, failure and recovery. These are not mandatory accessibility features.
checks.evidence: Offline/install scenario with cache/recovery behavior.

checks.title: Privacy-sensitive integrations
checks.check: Review third-party behavior and applicable privacy choices with current organizational policy. Preserve the old DNT item as historical input, not a sufficient modern privacy control.
checks.evidence: Current policy decision and integration evidence.

checks.title: Print and downloadable documents
checks.check: If print or downloads are in scope, provide usable equivalents and refer PDFs to a dedicated document-accessibility process. Tags alone do not prove an accessible PDF; do not hide meaningful interactive content from print without an equivalent.
checks.evidence: Print/download review or documented specialist handoff.

checks.title: AI asset approval workflow
checks.check: Preserve the supplied content/design AI review steps as an organization-specific policy to validate with its current owner; do not execute historical contact instructions or assume they still apply.
checks.evidence: Current policy reference and approval record if applicable.

checks.title: Visual fallback and existing content
checks.check: Check hero/background fallback, image clarity, overlapping/default elements and existing/shared components after updates. Test contrast independently, including when assets fail.
checks.evidence: Normal/failure render and changed/pre-existing element regression.

checks.title: Optional visual style preferences
checks.check: Treat above-field labels, avoiding pure black/white and strong prescribed affordance styles as design decisions. Evaluate outcomes and user needs rather than enforcing inherited recipes universally.
checks.evidence: Documented design policy and usability evidence.

actions.content: Choose appropriate data, simplify, author headers/units/caption and an understandable explanation.
actions.design: Specify reading relationships, visual grouping, narrow/zoom layouts and interaction states.
actions.dev: Implement table associations and the selected static-table or interactive-grid behavior.
actions.system: Provide safe primitives, slots/props and documented sorting/selection/focus responsibilities.
actions.qa: Verify header associations, sorting/selection, keyboard access and narrow/AT tasks.
actions.research: Test whether people can locate and interpret important values using their access strategies.
actions.locale: Validate translated headers/units, number formats, long strings and direction.

actions.content: Write labels, instructions, errors, recovery suggestions and confirmation text.
actions.design: Specify grouped flow, required/invalid presentation, focus and error placement.
actions.dev: Associate labels/errors; expose required/invalid states; implement recovery and submission.
actions.system: Document accessible defaults versus consumer duties, including form association.
actions.qa: Test valid, invalid, repeated-entry, correction and consequential-submit paths.
actions.research: Evaluate comprehension, effort, authentication and recovery barriers.
actions.locale: Review local names/addresses, translated feedback and label/name consistency.

actions.content: Decide purpose and author contextual short/long alternatives.
actions.design: Preserve meaning beyond color and plan accessible equivalent views.
actions.dev: Use the right alternative/name hooks without redundant or hidden semantics.
actions.system: Expose safe decorative/informative icon/image APIs and examples.
actions.qa: Review actual purpose, rendered alternatives and complex-data task equivalence.
actions.research: Evaluate whether alternatives support the same important interpretation.
actions.locale: Translate alternatives and localize embedded data/units.

actions.content: Plan accurate captions, transcripts, descriptions and media names.
actions.design: Specify controls, pause/reduced-motion behavior and non-motion alternatives.
actions.dev: Implement accessible controls, preferences and timing behavior.
actions.system: Provide accessible player/motion defaults and documented consumer duties.
actions.qa: Check playback, keyboard, alternatives, preferences and flashing where applicable.
actions.locale: Localize synchronized text, descriptions and controls.
actions.delivery: Budget and schedule accessible media production.

actions.content: Write a meaningful outline, titles, links and navigation labels.
actions.design: Specify relationships, reading/focus sequences and consistent navigation.
actions.dev: Preserve structure and order in rendered semantics and routing.
actions.system: Support correct section/landmark and navigation compositions.
actions.qa: Verify structure, bypass and reading/keyboard journeys.
actions.research: Evaluate findability and comprehension rather than inferring them from markup.
actions.locale: Validate localized names, outlines and direction.

actions.content: Write names, instructions, state and status messages.
actions.design: Select pattern/variant, specify keys, focus, targets, hidden/disabled behavior and status intent.
actions.dev: Implement actual behavior, focus and programmatic semantics.
actions.system: Supply tested pattern primitives and versioned accessibility contracts.
actions.qa: Exercise all important states with keyboard, pointer and selected AT.
actions.research: Evaluate task success, discoverability and predictability with participants.

actions.content: Keep content understandable under expansion, text alternatives and reordered presentation.
actions.design: Specify contrast, state cues, typography and adaptive layouts.
actions.dev: Honor browser/OS preferences and preserve content/function under adaptation.
actions.system: Provide robust tokens, themes and safe component states.
actions.qa: Measure and exercise contrast, zoom, spacing, orientation and forced colors.
actions.locale: Stress long strings, glyph coverage, wrapping and direction.
actions.research: Validate readability and task outcomes under participants’ settings.

actions.locale: Own locale/direction coverage and linguistic review.
actions.content: Supply translatable visible and accessible-only content with context.
actions.design: Plan expansion, wrapping, direction and local conventions.
actions.dev: Implement lang/dir, locale behavior and translated semantics.
actions.system: Provide locale-capable components and accessible string hooks.
actions.qa: Run per-locale tasks and verify destinations, names and layouts.

corrections: Scope and provenance

The referenced full WCAG worksheet/master spreadsheet is not one of the supplied files. Planning summaries and a cheat sheet cannot establish complete WCAG coverage. The proposed profile is 2.2 A/AA; historical 2.1 and later MVP 2.2 notes coexist.
Keep a coverage ledger and obtain/reconcile the actual master worksheet before asserting completeness.
Heading count and straplines
One h1 is a useful page convention; count alone is not a universal WCAG failure. A real subsection may warrant a heading, whatever the editorial name strapline.
STR02: judge actual section structure; retain site policy separately.
Images and alternatives
The alt-tag how-to footnote repeats a file-size instruction. Empty alt for a decorative img and aria-hidden are not interchangeable in every context; do not hide a focusable control.
IMG01: classify purpose and test the actual library output; use provider defaults, such as decorative RHDS icons.
Disabled and hidden controls
Native disabled controls usually leave sequential focus; aria-disabled composite items can remain discoverable/focusable. Intentionally visually hidden text may remain accessible.
INT05: define the state and widget contract before applying a rule.
Messages and dialogs
Not every error/status requires a new live region. Modal initial focus and return are contextual; nonmodal overlays must not inherit modal trapping.
INT04/INT09/FRM02: distinguish focus, association, state and announcement.
Typography, units and targets
Relative units, font choice, label position and avoiding pure black/white are methods or design policies. AA target size has exceptions; larger targets may be a product goal.
VIS04/INT07/POL01: assess outcomes and label authority rather than enforcing one CSS recipe.
200% is not the whole adaptation check
Text resize and reflow are separate checks. Some two-dimensional table content is exempt from reflow, while surrounding content still needs it.
VIS03/TAB03: test resize, narrow viewport, text spacing and table scrolling separately.
Language and navigation policy
A CMS language list is not the boundary of valid HTML language metadata. Same-window navigation and warnings for every external link are site conventions, not universal AA obligations.
LOC01/TXT03: expose actual language and evaluate unexpected behavior.
Older web technology recommendations

Service workers/manifests are optional product architecture. Image type alone does not establish forced-color support. DNT is historical; font subsetting and honeypots need product-specific evaluation.
WEB08–10/VIS05/FRM03: retain intent; do not turn legacy advice into universal requirements.
General QA and automation claims
S3 p1; S4 auto-QA column; S5 p6; H065
Visual regression is not keyboard/AT verification. Historical adoption targets are not current goals. PDF tags are necessary in many workflows but insufficient alone.
QA02–07/WEB11: record exactly what was observed or delegated.
roadmap: Canonical checks and role-task views
Store stable IDs, source/version, authority, applicability, role actions and evidence requirements. Generate short, detailed and export views from one record.
One corrected table rule appears consistently in content/design/dev/QA views; duplicate source wording remains traceable.
Shared topic packages
Start with tables, forms/errors, media, structure and visual alternatives. Keep meaning, design intent, implementation and verification linked.
A table has one contract and role-specific work, not four contradictory checklist copies.
Provider bindings
Bind shared checks to versioned PF React/HTML, RHDS WC and future Felt React/WC docs/APIs; runtime selection remains separate.
Switch providers without replacing the table meaning or evidence contract.
Workflow and authoring integration
Load applicable checks for role + task + stage + target; make exported checklists, skill references and authoring prompts use the same catalog.
Screenshot reviews cannot mark runtime checks passed; CMS-specific analytics rules never become shared WCAG rules.
Research, verification and governance
Add accessible participation, observed task evidence, dated support matrices, source owners and retest/upkeep. Preserve historical plans as context.
Research observations remain distinct from expert/automated evidence; updates retain stable IDs and assigned owners.
